description.value: The study examined how behavioral inhibition and activation motivation dispositions modulate neural responses during cognitive reappraisal in currently drug-free patients with major depressive disorder compared with healthy controls.

design.value: A between-subjects fMRI study using a block-designed emotional picture task with three consecutive conditions—ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE—and positive, negative, and neutral stimuli; the order of DETACH and IMMERSE was counterbalanced across participants.

name.value: Behavioral Inhibition System and Behavioral Activation System Scale (BBS)

description.value: A revised Chinese version of the scale measuring BIS, BASR, BASD, and BASF motivation dispositions, administered immediately after the scan.
A 21-item self-rating scale of emotional, cognitive, motivational and somatic symptoms, scored from 0 to 3.
A 20-item self-rated scale of psychological and somatic symptoms, scored from 1 to 4.
An interview scale used to measure severity of depression.
Participants rated emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale after each picture.

source_definition.value: BIS subscale score from the BBS
BAS-drive subscale score from the BBS
BAS-reward responsiveness subscale score from the BBS
BAS-fun seeking subscale score from the BBS

description.value: Twelve currently drug-free, major depressed outpatients with a major depressive episode.

exclusion_criteria.value: history of neurological disease or presence of axis I psychiatric disorders
no use of psychiatric medicine for at least 2 weeks

recruitment_method.value: recruited and evaluated by structured clinical interview for DSM-IV-TR Axis I (SCID I); screened via diagnoses from an experienced psychiatric clinician according to DSM-IV-TR

clinical_characteristics.value: HAMD-24: 25.17 ± 5.18; BDI: 26.17 ± 12.65; SDS: 64.08 ± 12.60; number of previous episodes: 1 in 9/12 patients, 2 in 2/12 patients, 3 in 1/12 patients

medication_status.value: currently drug-free; no use of psychiatric medicine for at least 2 weeks

description.value: Fifteen healthy controls with no current or past axis I disorders and no first-degree family history of MDD, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia.

exclusion_criteria.value: current or past axis I disorders and first-degree family history of MDD, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia

recruitment_method.value: recruited and evaluated by structured clinical interview for DSM-IV-TR Axis I (SCID I)

medical_condition.value: no current or past axis I disorders

task_description.value: Participants viewed emotional pictures in three consecutive blocks: ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE. ATTEND required responding naturally; DETACH required interpreting the situation as fake or unreal; IMMERSE required perceiving each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.

instructions.value: During ATTEND, subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state. During DETACH, participants interpreted the situation depicted as fake or unreal. During IMMERSE, subjects perceived each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.

stimuli.value: Pictures selected from the International Affective Picture System; positive, negative, and neutral emotional pictures.

task_performance_measures.value: self-reported ratings of emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Three functional sessions were acquired. Visual stimuli were presented through goggles mounted on the head coil.

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: A T1-weighted MPRAGE structural image was acquired.
The first trial of each block was discarded; remaining volumes were slice-time corrected, realigned to the mean volume, spatially normalized to standard MNI space, and smoothed.

steps.value: The first trial of each block was discarded to reach magnetization equilibrium.
Realignment to the mean volume to correct for head motion.
Spatial normalization to standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation.
Smoothing by convolution with a standard 8-mm full-width at half-maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: Each condition was modeled using a box-car function convolved with a canonical HRF; realignment parameters were included as covariates of no interest.

Group, emotion and ER were between-subject factors and BIS/BAS subscale scores were covariates; interactive effects between group and motivation and the main effect of group on emotion regulation were examined.
BIS/BAS scores were entered to predict reappraisal-related brain activation using ROI time courses (beta values).
BBS subscale scores were compared between groups.

description.value: Subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state elicited by the stimuli; this was the baseline condition.
Avoidance-oriented reappraisal: participants interpreted the situation depicted as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events.
Approach-oriented reappraisal: subjects perceived each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.
Positive emotional pictures.
Negative emotional pictures.
Neutral pictures, presented only under the ATTEND condition.
